name: Masked Man Fallacy
description: A reasoner substitutes one label for another inside a belief- or knowledge-based context as if identity automatically preserves truth, even when the person in the story would not make that substitution. It is a textbook logic problem about reference and knowledge, not a clearly established named cognitive-bias effect.
design_relevance_note: Only very niche relevance to identity, personalization, permissions, knowledge-representation, or AI-reasoning work where co-referring labels get treated as interchangeable in belief contexts. For mainstream digital product design it is mostly too formal and logic-specific to matter day to day.
prevalence_note: A specialized logic/philosophy term with little visible uptake in ordinary design discourse; at most it surfaces in unusually formal reasoning or knowledge-modeling discussions.
